newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican Catholic says church paid for her abortion.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican Catholic says church paid for her abortion.

text.p: A Catholic woman who fell pregnant during a love affair with a priest told South Africa's parliament on Wednesday that a senior churchman paid for her abortion.
The woman said she felt compelled to speak out against what she called the church's hypocrisy, for calling abortion a sin, but paying her medical bills.

South Africa's parliament, which decided that the woman's identity should remain secret, is holding public debates on a proposed law that would allow abortion on demand up to the 12th week and for a further eight weeks in some circumstances.
The witness, who called on MPs to adopt the new law, said she had an "intimate emotional and sexual relationship" with a Catholic priest in 1994.
It ended a year later, but by then she was pregnant.
The woman said she did not have the money to raise a child on her own and had unsuccessfully sought help from the church.
"At no point did any member of the Catholic hierarchy who was aware of my special circumstances intervene or offer to help me so that it could prevent me having an abortion.

"After my abortion a member of the hierarchy wrote me a cheque which covered my hospital and doctor's bills," she said, adding that she would have kept the child if she had been given financial support for it.
Friends of the woman, who was accompanied by a bodyguard, said she had received anonymous death threats from people trying to stop her from testifying.
Two other Catholic women earlier broke ranks with the church's official abortion line, urging parliament to adopt the new law.

Mary Armour, who testified at an earlier hearing, said her pro-choice stance was not unusual, but silenced in the church by the unmarried priests who run it. The Catholic church opposes abortion for any reason and has called on the South African government to probe the underlying reasons for illegal backstreet abortions in South Africa.
"To refuse women access to contraception as well as abortion is inhumane," said Armour, a theology graduate.
Catholic church representative Noel Pistorius said any surgical or medical ending of pregnancy was an "infringement of an inalienable right to life and consequently gravely immoral."
Christian anti-abortion campaigners have repeatedly clashed with some members of parliament over the proposed law, which they say ignores majority opinion.
At present about 1,000 women a year qualify for legal abortions allowed under circumstances such as rape, incest and danger to the mother's life.
